ownership.why: The four loader projects in THIS repository glob `..\FusionRpg.Injector\Assets\actor-hud-elements\**\*.png` (FusionRpg.Injector.BepInEx.csproj, .MelonLoader.csproj, .MelonLoader.39.csproj, .MelonLoader.40.csproj), so this tree is the build input and the shipped bytes originate here. gk-web's web/fusion-rpg-web/public/actor-hud-elements/ is downstream of it.
ownership.noCodeReadsThisFile: No .cs, .csproj, .py, .ts or .tsx file in the workspace names this manifest. The project files glob *.png only, so it is not shipped in a build either. It is a provenance and normalisation record; the source prompt, the alpha sampling notes and the crop rule below exist nowhere else. Treat it as a record, not as a runtime contract.
ownership.fileNamingIsTheContract: Both consumers resolve a glyph by NAMING CONVENTION and not by this file: ActorHudElementArt.cs combines `assets/actor-hud-elements` with `hudGlyph + ".png"`, and gk-web's actorHudElementArtUrl returns `/actor-hud-elements/${hudGlyph}.png`. So a glyph's file is `<hudGlyph>.png` at the tree root, and the `assets[].path` column below restates that convention rather than describing a mapping anything reads.
ownership.elementTableOwner: The `assets[]` rows' elementId / hudGlyph / catalogColor restate gk-core's data/tuning/element-catalog.v2.json `entries` fields id / hudGlyph / color, value for value. That catalog is the OWNER and is authoritative; the table below is a SNAPSHOT taken at generation time. If they ever disagree, the catalog wins and this file is the stale one.

downstreamCopy.mechanism: MANUAL COPY. There is no mirror, sync or checksum tool for this tree in any repository, and no test compares the two copies. A change to a PNG here is NOT picked up there automatically.
downstreamCopy.stateAsOf2026_10_05: The 64px root set and this manifest are byte-identical between the two repositories (all 7 files, SHA-256 compared). gk-web's copy holds the root 64px set ONLY and therefore does not contain the 128/ and 256/ tiers that `availableCanvasPixels` below lists — a manifest declaring files that repository does not carry.
downstreamCopy.whyTheSubsetIsNotDrift: Neither consumer requests a tier: ActorHudElementArt.cs loads the root PNGs and gk-web's URL template names the root PNGs. The 128 and 256 tiers have no reader in either repository today; the `variants` descriptions below call them reserved for FE display. Adding them to gk-web would cost ~360 KB in a web bundle for a tier nothing asks for.

source.prompt: Premium hand-painted arcane energy crest tokens, designed for a readable 64px actor HUD. Fire: scarlet/orange angular combustion crest; Ice: cyan/white crystalline frost crest; Air: turquoise vortex crest; Earth: ochre/emerald fractured geomantic crest; Light: gold/white vertical radiant prism, never a sun or star; Dark: violet/indigo fractured void rift, never a moon or crescent. Transparent background, no text.

normalization.crop: per-element alpha bounds, expanded 14% to preserve the energy silhouette

variants.64: root PNG files; Unity runtime source
